02 / A CONNECTED WAY OF WORKING

Different industries. A familiar geospatial pattern.

Environmental consultants, resilience teams, utilities, and location-intelligence teams ask different business questions, but the work often repeats the same underlying pattern: find or bring the right data, prepare it, run spatial analysis, check assumptions, review the result, and communicate what the map means for the decision.

GriidAi is designed to connect those steps so expert methods do not have to be rebuilt from scratch for every new project or location.

04 / FROM QUESTION TO RESULT

Keep the industry context. Keep the expert in control.

Industry context changes the data, assumptions, thresholds and interpretation of a spatial analysis. GriidAi can help organize and execute supported steps, while the expert reviews the plan and validates the outcome before it informs a decision.

  1. 01

    Define

    State the spatial question, study area, time window and intended use.

  2. 02

    Data

    Bring your own layers or use a supported source. Inspect coverage and metadata.

  3. 03

    Plan

    See the proposed inputs, method, validation and expected output.

  4. 04

    Review

    Check assumptions, units, parameters and the selected data before execution.

  5. 05

    Execute

    Run the approved, supported spatial operations.

  6. 06

    Validate

    Inspect maps, tables, statistics and intermediate results.

  7. 07

    Continue

    Export, refine or carry the result into the next analytical step.

07 / HUMAN-GUIDED RELIABILITY

Spatial decisions need more than a plausible map

AI proposes the work. Experts control what proceeds.

A plausible map can still be wrong when the projection, time window, units, selected data or analytical assumption is wrong. Review the plan before processing and validate the mapped or tabular result before using it.
